newsitem.title: UK: Major says wants Lockerbie trial in Scotland or US.
newsitem.headline: Major says wants Lockerbie trial in Scotland or US.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday he wanted to see two Libyans suspected of planting the Lockerbie airliner bomb which killed 270 people tried in Scotland or the United States.
"I believe the trial should either be in Scotland, which is the preference, or the United States," Major told parliament.

Two Libyan agents have been indicted in the United States and Britain for planting a bomb that blew up Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie in Scotland, killing all of the 259 people on board and 11 people on the ground.

"We would like a solution as much as the relatives but we need a proper criminal trial and there are genuine and practical difficulties in trying to establish such a trial in a third country," Major said.

Conservative MP Teddy Taylor said the Libyan government has said it will hand over the two for trial in the Hague "or anywhere else". He noted senior Scottish lawyers have said it would be impossible for the two to have a fair trial because of media publicity.
But Major said he would find trial in a third country very difficult to accept as it would suggest a trial in Scotland or the United States could not be fair.

"Neither do I think it would be remotely attractive for us to allow alleged terrorists to dictate where they may or may not be tried," he said. "I am very doubtful the Libyans would deliver the accused to such a trial, even if one were set up."
The United Nations has imposed sanctions on Libya for refusing to hand over the two men for trial in the United States or Britain.
